Standards support

Offing keys every lifecycle rule by Package URL (PURL) and VERS. It exports and ingests CLE, enriches CycloneDX SBOMs, and emits SARIF. CycloneDX and SPDX input checking exists only as an internal library API today — no CLI, GitHub Action, MCP tool, or detector exposes it. Scans stay offline: they read repository files and bundled (or pinned) data only.

Support table

Standard Role in Offing Status How to use it
PURL Component identity Supported Every rule’s purl (version-less); offing check pkg:…; CLE identifiers; CycloneDX enrichment matching
VERS Affected version ranges Supported Every rule’s vers; CLE versions[].range; matching in scans, checks, and CycloneDX enrichment
CLE (ECMA-428) Lifecycle interchange Supported Export: offing export --format cle. Ingest: maintainer cle.json in installed packages during offing scan
CycloneDX SBOM enrichment Supported offing sbom enrich <bom.json> (JSON 1.3–1.6)
CycloneDX SBOM input Library API only (no CLI command yet) No command, Action, or MCP tool exposes it yet
SPDX SBOM input Library API only (no CLI command yet) No command, Action, or MCP tool exposes it yet
SARIF 2.1.0 Findings output Supported offing scan --format sarif; GitHub Action upload-sarif: true
OpenEoX Vendor EOL policy Not read Decision 0017: CLE remains the interchange target until the OpenEoX Core Schema is final

PURL and VERS

Rules in registry/ use a canonical, version-less PURL and a VERS range. Detectors and offing check match an observed version against that range. The rule format, evidence policy, and examples are in Lifecycle rules; the design is Decision 0004.

offing check pkg:npm/request@2.88.2
offing check pkg:generic/nodejs@18.20.0
{
  "purl": "pkg:npm/request",
  "vers": "vers:npm/*"
}

Runtimes without a registry type use pkg:generic/<name> (for example pkg:generic/nodejs). VERS schemes follow the component: npm, pypi, semver, and the other schemes listed in Decision 0004.

CLE (ECMA-428)

CLE is the lifecycle document format Offing exports and, when a maintainer ships it, reads.

Export. Print one CLE 1.0 JSON document per component (NDJSON on stdout) from the active offline data:

offing export --format cle > lifecycle.ndjson

Only dated component-level end-of-support, end-of-life, and scheduled-end-of-life rules map faithfully. Soft deprecations, API removals, symbol-only rules, and undated rules are omitted; a count of skipped rules goes to stderr. Event versions[].range keeps the rule’s VERS string; identifier is the rule’s PURL. Output validates against the CLE 1.0 schema.

Ingest. During offing scan, Offing looks for cle.json next to package.json under node_modules. The document’s identifier must match the installed package as a PURL, and the installed version must fall in an event’s VERS range. How to ship a document: Declaring lifecycle for your package.

CycloneDX

Enrich. Add official cdx:lifecycle milestone properties and evidence URLs to a copy of a CycloneDX JSON BOM. The input file is never modified. Spec versions 1.3 through 1.6 are accepted. Components match by PURL (and version from the PURL or the component version field) against the same offline rules as dependency checks. Undated, symbol-only, and version-dependent claims are not written as milestones.

offing sbom enrich bom.json > bom.enriched.json

Example property names Offing may add:

  • cdx:lifecycle:milestone:endOfSupport
  • cdx:lifecycle:milestone:endOfLife

Input. Internal API only: scanCycloneDx / scanCycloneDxFile in src/sbom/input.ts. Nothing in the CLI, GitHub Action, MCP server, or any detector calls these functions, so there is no user-facing command to check a CycloneDX BOM today.

The library function checks each component that carries a purl with the same offline dependency API as offing check. Nested and metadata components are included; components without a PURL are skipped. Results stay explicit for no-data and version-dependent cases. Each result’s location is a JSON Pointer to that component (for example /components/0 or /metadata/component). A version embedded in the PURL wins over the component’s version field. Spec versions 1.3 through 1.6 are accepted.

{
  "bomFormat": "CycloneDX",
  "specVersion": "1.6",
  "components": [
    {
      "type": "library",
      "name": "request",
      "version": "2.88.2",
      "purl": "pkg:npm/request"
    }
  ]
}

SPDX

Internal API only: scanSpdx / scanSpdxFile in src/sbom/input.ts. Nothing in the CLI, GitHub Action, MCP server, or any detector calls these functions, so there is no user-facing command to check an SPDX document today.

The library function checks SPDX 2.3 JSON packages. For each package, it looks at externalRefs whose referenceType is purl (case-insensitive). A version in the PURL wins over versionInfo. Packages and refs without a PURL are skipped. The document is never written. Each result’s location is a JSON Pointer to the matched external reference (for example /packages/0/externalRefs/0); spdxId is set when the package has an SPDXID.

{
  "spdxVersion": "SPDX-2.3",
  "packages": [
    {
      "name": "request",
      "SPDXID": "SPDXRef-request",
      "versionInfo": "2.88.2",
      "externalRefs": [
        {
          "referenceCategory": "PACKAGE-MANAGER",
          "referenceType": "purl",
          "referenceLocator": "pkg:npm/request"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

SARIF

offing scan --format sarif emits deterministic SARIF 2.1.0. Paths are repository-relative with forward slashes; rules and results are sorted; no scan timestamp or absolute checkout path is written. The GitHub Action can upload the same file to code scanning (upload-sarif: true in action.yml). Field mapping and privacy notes: GitHub Action — SARIF output.

offing scan . --format sarif > offing.sarif

What Offing does not do with these standards

  • Scans never fetch CLE, SBOMs, or OpenEoX over the network.
  • There is no CLI, GitHub Action, or MCP command that checks a CycloneDX or SPDX SBOM as input; those helpers stay internal in src/sbom/input.ts.
  • CLE export does not invent end-of-life claims for soft deprecations or API removals.
  • CycloneDX enrichment never removes existing BOM fields; it only adds properties and documentation references.
  • OpenEoX documents are not ingested; see Decision 0017.
